argument_summary: The certification case should be interpreted narrowly. The admissible record supports a limited pro-certification packet based on aggregate readiness passing by 2.3 points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance principles permitting deployment with measured and documented residual risk. The same admissible record also shows the merchant dispute support segment misses target by 1.4 points, is named in two marketplace renewal commitments, and remains under open legal review on disclosure. That means the defensible position is not that the gap is clearly immaterial or that policy predicates are fully satisfied; it is that certification is arguable only as a caveated governance judgment resting on overall readiness plus explicit preservation of the unresolved limitation in the packet.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not required if the auditor can distinguish between rejecting a clean-compliance theory and accepting a narrower caveated-certification theory. The admissible record already preserves the contrary evidence, so a bounded caveat can reduce unnecessary rollout friction without overstating policy satisfaction. This is not a claim that business cost overrides policy; it is a claim that the existing record supports a narrower, less escalatory treatment than a full adverse inference.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not support treating the segment gap as resolved by a non-core or low-volume label, because the admissible record says the segment is named in customer commitments and legal review is pending. Public AI governance and model-card guidance can contextualize why residual risk may be managed at deployment, but they do not replace the internal policy predicates. On this record, the strongest policy-consistent framing is caveated compliance for certification review, not a clean statement that the limitation is immaterial or that disclosure obligations are definitively cleared.
concessions: The current record does not prove resolved legal review, completed disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
The merchant dispute support segment appears plausibly material under the stated policy because it is named in two marketplace renewal commitments.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves satisfy the internal disclosure policy.
The certification defense is weak to moderate and should not be presented as clean compliance.
